mathematical_map.raw_field: Z[i,j] = G[i,j] / E[i,j] away from the one-sparse boundary
mathematical_map.one_sparse_gradient: D is supported on the active cell with its sign and Frobenius norm rho(m,n)
mathematical_map.forbidden_epsilon: No additive epsilon is part of the optimizer map.

parameter_matrixization.rank_ge_3_tensor: reshape [axis0, product(axis1:)] with axis0 the semantic output or record axis
parameter_matrixization.tied_embedding_head: one shared [vocabulary,hidden] parameter transformed once after gradient accumulation
parameter_matrixization.sparse_layout: Materialize the mathematically equivalent dense gradient or implement an exactly equivalent sparse-support transform; do not fall back to another optimizer.

initial_decoder_contract.architecture: bias-free decoder-only Transformer with trainable normalization gains
parameter_groups: token embedding and tied/untied output head

steps: If every entry is zero, return exact zero.
If exactly one entry is nonzero, return the exact projective boundary direction.
Scale G by max(abs(G)) before squaring; this common positive scaling does not change the output ray.
Accumulate nonnegative row and column energies in fp32 or higher.
Compute outside-row and outside-column energy with exclusion-safe nonnegative reductions (for example prefix/suffix reductions), not cancellation-prone 2*S-r-c subtraction near the boundary.
For each active entry compute E as outside_row + outside_column.
Let e_min be the smallest positive active denominator and compute raw[i,j] = scaled_G[i,j] * e_min / E[i,j]; set inactive raw entries to zero.

If an active denominator still rounds to zero, recompute affected exclusions in fp64; if the represented input has become exactly one-sparse, use the boundary branch, otherwise raise a numerical diagnostic rather than add epsilon.
Accumulate ||raw||_F in fp32 or higher and normalize once to rho(m,n).
finite_precision_execution.underflow_rule: exclusion-safe accumulation plus fp64 rare-path recomputation; exact represented one-sparse inputs use the declared boundary
